brand: Hunt for a sticky header band containing a compact inline typographic lockup with 3 horizontal tiers in one flex row: (1) a boxed micro-prefix in monospace+amber with hairline border, (2) a display-weight uppercase wordmark with amber highlight on one syllable only, (3) a spaced mono sub-label at a smaller size — all baseline-aligned, NOT stacked vertically and NOT centered on the page

Structural tell: the badge uses a hairline border + slightly elevated panel background making it a distinct chromatic node without being decorative; the amber partial on tier 2 echoes the badge color without doubling it; both amber hits together are ≤2 nodes in the full lockup
Reject: centered hero branding, full-width brand color bands, logos with padding zones, any treatment where brand floats outside header flow or amber fills the entire masthead background
step-heads: Hunt for a baseline-aligned flex row of [number marker] + [div with title+desc] where the number is a raw monospace amber '0N' label — no circle, no pill, no icon, no background fill, no stroke ring — and the title uses a condensed/display face at ~25px uppercase, with the desc in smaller body weight below

The CSS ::before prepends '0' to make '1'→'01' purely via content property; hunt for references that treat step numbers as typographic counters rather than progress-indicator shapes — the number's function is section-label, not stepper-stage

Structural tell: the step-body is a hairline-bordered panel-bg rectangle that follows immediately below the step-head with a gap — this makes the number+title a section divider, not a wizard-flow stage; reject any numbered-steps reference that implies linearity with connectors or progress fills
terminal-preview: Hunt for a terminal window frame embedded mid-page (between sticky header and form sections) with: (a) a titlebar containing traffic-light dots where only one dot has fill (amber/accent) and the other two are empty hairline circles; (b) a centered uppercase mono title in the titlebar; (c) a range slider right-aligned in the titlebar for column-width with an amber-accented badge readout; (d) a content area on a background DARKER than the outer container

Structural tell: the window carries an inset box-shadow at ~6% amber opacity — a barely-there amber inset glow at the interior edge, not an outer glow ring; this is the restraint signal to hunt for specifically

Accept titlebar layouts where the col-width badge is a mono amber label in a hairline box flush with the slider — this control is structurally part of the titlebar chrome, not a caption below the window; reject terminal frames where the width control is external to the titlebar band

acceptNuance: Accept UIs where a faint 1px engineering substrate grid (~46px repeat) is visible through the page background as a deliberate textural signal of instrument-grade design — this is not a layout grid artifact and should be weighted positively

Accept step-head patterns where the number is typographically raw with no container shape — the absence of a circle or badge around '01' is the specific restraint marker; reject any reference wrapping step numbers in colored chips, filled circles, or outlined pills

Accept terminal preview titlebar dots that are deliberately asymmetric: 2 empty hairline circles + 1 amber-filled circle — this asymmetry is the design intent, not an incomplete mockup; reject references with uniformly colored dot rows or rainbow traffic lights
Accept near-zero radius throughout (≤3px) as an instrument-sharpness signal — the rejection threshold for rounded-card aesthetic is ≥8px; 2px radius reads as sharp, purposeful, and operator-grade

Accept brand mastheads where amber appears in at most 2 specific typographic nodes out of the full lockup — amber as area fill or background wash for the masthead band is a rejection signal even on otherwise dark UIs
